acceptance_notes: Accepted run_04 of 8 candidates (2 rounds of 4) after Reading every raw sheet, review.png and a scratch ingest preview of each candidate (SSP-014, decision D-04). PROVENANCE TRADE-OFF: the probe candidate (assets-src/_probe/codex/old_woman_sheet.png, the previous golden.png) could only ever carry a retro meta.json (prompt_sha256 and preamble_version null, the model inferred rather than pinned, argv reconstructed), which falls short of the M0 deliverable 'golden with complete provenance' and of VS-5 (every AI golden in use has a complete meta.json). It also failed the Doris review on its own merits: no shopping trolley (the signature silhouette is hunch + trolley), no headscarf, a brown rather than maroon handbag, a face hidden under the hair (its 14x18 ingest kept a 1 px skin strip and no eyes) and walk frames that are not a cycle. A fresh forge gen-ai generation cost about 8 minutes of Codex time (8 x 53-116 s) plus review, inside the ADR 0002 5.2 budget of 3 rounds, and gives complete provenance (pinned -m, prompt.md hashed, preamble v1), so the fresh generation was chosen. WHY run_04 WON: the chunkiest, cleanest pixel grid of all 8 (colour run lengths are modal at 13-14 px on both axes, with doubles at 27-28 px), so its native figures are 18-21 art px and the one sheet step-down is 0.9048, the closest to 1 of any candidate (round 1: 0.41-0.54; the probe: 0.58). It holds the whole Doris colour key (headscarf 31, coat 31 lit over 30, maroon handbag 19, red/navy tartan trolley 18/25, grey hair 06, skin 12/11), a trolley in every cell on a consistent side, a correct S/SW/W/NW/N turnaround, a 1 px dark outline, real alpha, no ground or cast shadow, no text, logos or brand-like marks. The wrapper verified it byte-identical to the thread's exec-3df266d3 image_gen output with no drawing commands (the agent generated twice in that thread, 98.5 s; the copied file is the first exec image listed in verify.json). CAVEATS: (1) the detected period is 14.30 x 12.10 px (the FFT detector picks a harmonic in x, which ADR 0002 5.1 flags as anisotropic), so ingest.json commits period_override 13.5 from the run-length measurement above; (2) the mouth is drawn as an X (the brief's 'cross mouth' was read literally); the grid replaces it with a 2 px mouth and later human prompts should ask for 'a small frowning mouth line'; (3) the front row is drawn about 10% shorter than row 2, so idle:s:0 lands 17 px tall against ART_BIBLE 7.2's 18-19 for elderly (left as is, inside the 18x22 limit); (4) the camera reads as the classic three-quarter character view (face full on, top of the headscarf visible), which is ART_BIBLE 4.4's high three-quarter cheat, not the straight-down reject of ASSET_PIPELINE 11.1 (that row applies to objects); the hunch shows in the side views more than the front row. REJECTED, round 1 (run_00-run_03; prompt revised after this round rather than looping): run_00 coat shaded near-black with many interior ink lines that ingest into an ink mass at a 0.43 factor, and an anisotropic 6.87 x 7.79 px period; run_01 the same dark coat at 0.54, a cute ':3' mouth instead of a cross one and the trolley swapped sides in the N cell; run_02 the best glare (angry brows) but a near-black coat and 36-44 px natives (factor 0.43), so face and coat collapse to ink; run_03 dark coat, 0.41 factor, a drooping sad face and a tilted trolley in the W cell. Round 2 (brighter coat, very low resolution, almost no interior lines): run_05 a good glare and palette but 23-31 px natives (factor 0.61) that lose the eyes and brows at 24x24, on a soft grid; run_06 an anisotropic 11.98 x 9.30 px period, figures only 12 px wide after scaling, X mouths and a tiny trolley; run_07 a clean 7.16 x 7.61 px period but a 0.63 factor that loses the face, red open mouths and leaning trolleys in the W and NW cells.
